# Benchmark Methodology

Curated by Skill Harbor: turn a scoped competitor set into comparable, defensible scores. Each competitor is assessed on the same nine dimensions with explicit 1-5 evidence-anchored rubrics, then captured in a uniform profile card; consistency is the point, scores are only useful if the same evidence would earn the same number for any competitor. The nine dimensions sum to 100% and guide synthesis emphasis, not a single blended score (avoid the false composite): positioning clarity and distinctiveness (18%), brand voice and verbal distinctiveness (15%), visual craft, offer packaging, evidence, enterprise-readiness, thought leadership, pricing, and the client's strategic tension. Dimension 9 is always the client's named tension; its two poles are scored separately and never averaged, because the strategic question is precisely whether a rival achieves both simultaneously. Runs after competitive-platform-analysis (which produces the scoped, tiered competitor set) and before competitive-report-structure (which assembles the profile cards). By @affaan-m, listed here with credit to its creator. From the affaan-m/ECC repository (MIT). Honest caveats: this needs a scoped, tiered competitor set first, it does not do the scoping; scores are evidence-anchored working documents, not verdicts, and the rubric is only as good as the evidence fed in. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use.
